title: PandamStyle benchmark corpus manifest
description: The identity of one generated corpus. Written next to the corpus it describes. Two runs are comparable only when their contentHash matches. Everything in `files` is hashed, so the manifest cannot claim a corpus it did not produce.

generator.description: The generator that produced the corpus. `commit` is the only field excluded from the determinism comparison.

parameters.description: The complete input to the generator. Given these five integers, the corpus is determined.

contentHash.description: sha256 over every generated file, path and content hash, in path order. This is the corpus identity.

designSystemHash.description: sha256 of the design-system definition alone, so a token-only change is distinguishable from a page-only change.

counts.description: What the corpus actually contains, counted by the generator rather than assumed. A corpus that cannot compile measures nothing, and these are the numbers that say whether it can.

expectedGraph.description: The module-graph shape the generator INTENDED. The MEASURED graph is recorded by the harness after a real build; the two are kept apart so a generator bug is visible instead of being confirmed by its own output.

expectedState.description: What the corpus is FOR. The positive project compiles and publishes; each negative trace must fail closed. The exact codes are asserted by the negative scenarios, not here, so a policy change cannot silently move the goalposts in the fixture.

files.description: Every generated file, sorted by path, with its byte length and content hash.
